what_happened: The Karnataka High Court at Dharwad told the police on 8 October to take no coercive steps until 13 October against a BJP functionary and two supporters booked over Form 7s against voters in Belagavi, LiveLaw and Bar and Bench reported. A Congress block agent's complaint, as the police record it, alleges they handed about 198 fabricated Form 7s to the booth officer. On 13 October Justice Venkatesh Naik T stayed the investigation until the next hearing, citing a coordinate bench's stay in similar cases on 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. The Court allowed the State to seek to have the order modified or vacated, and posted the matter for 29 October.
commission_reply: The Government Pleader sought time to file objections and the latest investigation report.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar announced on 9 October that the Commission had decided to limit an individual voter to ten Form 7 objections for the whole claims and objections period and five a month during continuous updation, citing bulk objections on unsubstantiated grounds, IANS reported. The statement said registration officers would act against false objections under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

The Karnataka High Court stayed proceedings in two FIRs against two BJP booth agents accused over bulk Form 7s against voters in Bengaluru's Malleshwaram constituency, Bar and Bench reported. The judge said the FIRs looked premature because the registration officer had not yet decided the Form 7s.
commission_reply: The State said the allegations of impersonation and forgery needed investigation and that the agents filed more applications than allowed. The complainant's counsel said the bulk filing was a conspiracy aimed at OBC and SC/ST voters.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; Election Commission
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that in the Tarabganj and Pilibhit Assembly constituencies 90 per cent of Form 7 deletion requests were against Muslim voters, and that in Tarabganj 188 objections were filed under one name on the same date against voters of one booth. It said the published data give no identity of an objector beyond a name, so the objectors cannot be checked.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission and had no reply by publication. The report does not say how it determined the voters' religion.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; BJP; Trinamool Congress
what_happened: The Wire reported that on 16 January 2026, during West Bengal's extended claims period, the Commission told the state's Chief Electoral Officer in writing that the law set no limit on the number of Form 7 objections one voter could file, and that on 9 October it capped them at ten per voter for a whole claims period, in an instruction to every state. The October instruction cites a paragraph of the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 against entertaining objections presented in bulk by an individual, which the January letter did not mention. Reading the Chief Electoral Officer's daily bulletins, the report counts 3,143 objections from party agents by 20 January, 2,926 from BJP agents and 217 from Trinamool agents, and finds that 2,539 of them first appear in the bulletin dated the day after the extended window closed on 19 January.
commission_reply: The report says the Commission has not said whether objections filed in January will be looked at again.

what_happened: The Wire reported, citing The Hindu, that 4,263 of the 13,462 Form 7 applications Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer received between 31 August and 16 October, or 31.67%, had not been published in the Form 10 lists. The Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023 requires each objection to be listed publicly for seven days before an Electoral Registration Officer can act on it.
commission_reply: The Hindu reported that it sent questions to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office and had no response by the time of publication.

what_happened: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer replaced the weekly report of applications disposed of on 22 October, and officials told The Hindu that the figures published until then were wrong. The revised report shows 1,07,451 of 4,59,796 Form 6 applications for inclusion and 47,105 of 67,709 Form 7 applications disposed of from 31 August to 18 October, about 23% and 70%. The earlier report had shown 1,238 Form 6 disposals to 11 October. Tri Nagar is the only constituency with no Form 6 disposal recorded in any of the seven weeks.
commission_reply: The Hindu attributes the quoted explanation to an unnamed official and does not say which office the official works in. More than 3.5 lakh Form 6 applications were still to be disposed of. Claims close on 30 October, every application is to be disposed of by 30 November, and the final roll is due on 4 December.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka; Congress; BJP
what_happened: Karnataka received 2,28,917 Form 7 applications between 16 June and 22 October, 1,70,442 of them after 23 September, when the count stood at 58,475, The Indian Express reported from official data. The Chief Electoral Officer's office said every Form 7 received up to 23 September had been cleared on priority and that hearings for all 43.82 lakh voters sent notices were over. Bangalore Urban had the most submissions in the paper's table, 24,268. The ruling Congress has alleged that the BJP is misusing Form 7 to file objections in bulk.
commission_reply: After a Congress protest at the Chief Electoral Officer's office earlier this month, the Chief Electoral Officer directed Electoral Registration Officers to look into the allegations. The state BJP has rejected them. The final roll is due on 27 October.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Electoral Registration Officer; Election Commission; Congress
issues: Form 7; Names left off or deleted; Minorities
what_happened: Newslaundry found 4,390 names on Kichha's draft roll that are missing from the final roll published on 3 October. About 670 of them had Form 7 objections filed against them in August, 509 by a single BJP booth level agent, and the other 3,720 had no objection against them and were deleted on the ground of logical discrepancies. Of the 6,884 Form 7 objections accepted in Kichha, 5,359 were that agent's, and he filed more Form 7 objections than anyone else in Uttarakhand. He told Newslaundry that the Electoral Registration Officer at first refused his bulk objections and took them after he complained to the Election Commission by email, and Newslaundry could not verify what the email said. Form 10 data from the Chief Electoral Officer's office show 504 of his accepted objections with an acceptance date of 14 August, a day after claims and objections closed. Newslaundry reported that every name in his objections was Muslim. He said the party had received information that about 6,000 electors enrolled in Kichha were also enrolled in five nearby constituencies of Uttar Pradesh.
commission_reply: The Kichha Electoral Registration Officer, Gaurav Pandey, neither confirmed nor denied the agent's account, would not say whether the Commission had directed him, and said the deletions followed the Commission's rules. Newslaundry said the Commission acknowledged its questions and did not answer them, and that it had asked the Chief Electoral Officer why objections were accepted after the deadline. The Congress MLA for Kichha, Tilak Raj Behar, said the objections rested on false information. The report does not say how it established the electors' religion.

what_happened: The Dharavi police registered a case under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 against a resident who had submitted 24 Form 7 applications in one day in the 178-Dharavi constituency, above the Election Commission's limit of ten a day, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation said on 24 October, The Hindu reported. The corporation alleged that the applications carried false and incorrect information. Mumbai's draft rolls were published on 31 August and claims and objections ran to 26 October.
commission_reply: The report gives no account from the accused. Section 31 covers anyone who knowingly makes a false statement or declaration in connection with the roll.

issues: Form 7; Notices and hearings; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: At least 61,059 Form 7 applications seeking deletions from Karnataka's rolls were filed by Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers themselves, and none gives a reason for the deletion, which the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 require, The Hindu reported. Officers listed as the objectors said the system generated the forms with their digital signatures when electors sent notices for no mapping or logical discrepancies could not be reached at hearings and were marked ineligible. Only 192 such applications were filed between 24 August and 23 September, and more than 60,800 between 24 September and 22 October, including 10,105 on 22 October, the last day for disposal. The paper's chart puts more than 53,000 of the officers' applications in the week from 16 to 22 October, with the most on one day, 11,760, on 19 October. In every case the paper checked on the Commission's portal the elector had already been deleted, including electors against whom the application came after 23 September. In the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike South district officers filed 10,374 of 17,491 applications, and in at least 26 constituencies officers filed more than voters or third parties did.
commission_reply: The officers said they had been told to file Form 7 for electors who had shifted, had a duplicate entry, were underage, had died or were not citizens. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer. Rule 17 of the 1960 Rules says a claim or objection not lodged within the period or in the prescribed form and manner shall be rejected by the registration officer. The paper also found 13,808 fewer Form 7 applications for 24 September to 22 October in the Commission's Form 10 records than the Chief Electoral Officer's statements give.

what_happened: The Commission announced in May 2025 that it was building ECINET, one platform to bring together more than 40 of its apps and websites for voters, election officials and other users.
The Supreme Court recorded, from the documents before it, what the logical discrepancy category in West Bengal covered and that about 1.36 crore voters fell in it.
The Commission launched ECINET formally on 22 January 2026 and said its trial version had already been used during the Bihar election and the SIR.
Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer listed six checks that ECINET used to flag mapping discrepancies in the third phase, among them a sibling age gap under nine months.

After its full meeting on 26 September 2026 the Commission said field officers have access to ECINET by role, set up a committee with an independent expert to check ECINET against the law, and said new IT modules would first go to a committee of officers.
Booth officers in Bhopal told the Free Press Journal they were asked to upload 100 forms a day and could not, because the booth officers' app server was down or very slow.

issues: Notices and hearings; Software (ECINET/ERONET); Transparency of lists
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal Commission records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for deciding which flagged voters to summon had been made public.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission did not answer its question on how flagged voters were chosen, and that questions sent to the Commission and three state offices on testing and procedure went unanswered.

what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that on 29 December 2025 the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office told state officials in writing that the logical discrepancy software was faulty because the 2002 roll had not been digitised accurately.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

issues: Notices and hearings; Duplicates and errors
source: Siasat (IANS, citing officials of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal)
what_happened: Officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told IANS that the logical discrepancy check caught people who had falsely linked themselves to unrelated voters, and gave examples they said were found at hearings.

The New Indian Express reported that the Android version of the booth officers' app was updated 31 times between 13 November 2025 and 20 January 2026, with no user manual for the updates, and that officials relied on the app to learn what the revision allowed.
The same report quoted a Chennai booth officer who said the app often froze on her phone, so that data was lost or finished work had to be done again.

The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that two EROs it spoke to, with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that spellings such as Xalxo and Khalkho triggered a discrepancy. The Collective said this showed the Commission had misled the Supreme Court, where it said there was no automated generation of notices.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission had not responded by publication. It set its finding against the Commission's submission to the Court that "There is no automated generation of notices" and that officers were "signing them off after application of mind".

what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that in West Bengal the logical discrepancy check flagged five kinds of mismatch, from spelling differences between the Bengali 2002 roll and the English draft to age gaps with parents and grandparents.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; District Election Officer
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET since that morning, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 on the Commission's ECINET portal carried a new declaration asking whether the applicant or their parents or grandparents were in the electoral roll of the last SIR, although the statutory form had not been amended. It reported that although the section was not marked mandatory, applicants could not submit the form without completing it, and that the downloadable Form 6 on the same portal did not include it.
commission_reply: The EC did not respond to a request for comment and Legislative Department Secretary Rajiv Mani could not be reached despite repeated attempts.

what_happened: The Hindu reported that 13 days into the Karnataka SIR only 0.41% of enumeration forms had been submitted online, and that voters complained of captcha failures, server errors and an ECINet search that failed to find records appearing in the published rolls. It reported that online submission required a current mobile number linked to the voter's EPIC.
commission_reply: Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar said the process was still under way. However, the CEO did not comment on the technical glitches reported by voters.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that people filling in enumeration forms on ECINET in Telangana kept being sent back to the home page, and an official put it down to the load from voters in more than a dozen states at once.

issues: Form 6; Commission's independence; Documents and declaration
what_happened: The Indian Express reported, from internal records it investigated, that on May 16 Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded that Form 6 is prescribed by statute and cannot be altered without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19. It reported that the declaration was added to the online form anyway, and that on August 13 Sandhu wrote that the changes were unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately.

The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi warned on file, from November 2025 to August 2026, that control of the electoral roll software was being centralised in the Commission's IT division. It reported that on August 14 Sandhu wrote that many Chief Electoral Officers, District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that on July 29 both Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.
commission_reply: The Election Commission and the two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, did not respond to calls and questionnaires emailed by The Indian Express seeking comment.

what_happened: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase of the SIR, up from four when the concept was introduced in West Bengal. They include a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Goa; Election Commission
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Notices and hearings; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINET because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21 and were still missing on September 20.
commission_reply: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told the paper the decision not to include them was the Commission's. The Indian Express later reported that the Commission said, after its meeting of 26 September, that 81 of the 97 had filled Form 6 and that the Chief Electoral Officer had been told to help include them.

what_happened: Commission officials said ECINET is decentralised, that each field officer acts through their own login, and that nobody at headquarters can perform those officers' statutory functions. ERONET is now part of ECINET.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Names left off or deleted; Notices and hearings
what_happened: The Hindu reported that more than 350 Delhi electors had been marked ineligible within a month of hearings, about 200 of them in Vikaspuri, and officials said the marking could not be rolled back by the registration officer or the state's Chief Electoral Officer.
commission_reply: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer wrote to officers on 25 September 2026 setting a 10-point checklist before marking anyone ineligible and telling them not to delete names on flimsy or frivolous grounds.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; Election Commission
what_happened: Outlook, citing NDTV, reported that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam asked for four changes to the ECINET software and more discretion for registration officers in logical discrepancy cases.
commission_reply: The Commission said on 26 September that several portal upgrades had already been made on inputs from state Chief Electoral Officers and that further flexibility needed by field officers would be made operational.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that on the night of 29 to 30 September 2026 the Commission removed the SIR declaration from the online Form 6 on ECINET for states where the final SIR rolls have been published. It reported that the declaration remained for states where the SIR is still ongoing.
commission_reply: The article cites the Commission's September 26 announcement that ‘for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used’.

what_happened: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that by restricting registration officers' access to the ECINet roll system and overruling them in Goa, West Bengal and other states, the Commission broke the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
commission_reply: PTI recalled that the Commission, under fire over objections from two of its Commissioners, had said differing views are a normal part of deliberation and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

issues: Form 6; Names left off or deleted; Documents and declaration
what_happened: The Indian Express reported a letter of 29 September from the Commission’s Secretary ordering a special drive to enrol "left out and young/first time eligible electors" in the 20 states and union territories where the revision is complete, using the statutory Form 6, with the added declaration kept for the revision phase only. It reported that at a video conference with all Chief Electoral Officers, the states were told to compare the roll from before the revision with the one after, list those left off or deleted, visit them at home and help those left out fill in Form 6, with help from the parties’ booth agents.
commission_reply: The letter of 29 September itself was not found. The Commission's letter of 1 October, which continues it, is in the timeline above. The Commission’s press note of 26 September, in the timeline above, had already ordered the drive, and Uttarakhand’s Chief Electoral Officer set out its steps in a press note of 3 October.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi
what_happened: The Hindu reported that the options reached Delhi officers on 30 September and only the ten states and union territories where the third phase was still under way, and that a case marked ineligible still could not be reversed.
commission_reply: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

issues: Form 6; Documents and declaration; Commission's independence
what_happened: Rahul Gandhi of the Congress, the Leader of the Opposition, said the Chief Election Commissioner had changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. The Commission replied on X that the statement was misleading, that its Bihar order of 24 June 2025 had the Commission's unanimous approval and was upheld by the Supreme Court on 27 May 2026, and that its press note of 26 September said the declaration attached to Form 6 had been upheld, Business Today reported.

The Indian Express reported that at a meeting on 11 August 2026 more than a dozen West Bengal appeal tribunal judges recorded that the Commission's portal did not let them serve notices, hold virtual hearings, restore a deleted voter or give appellants a copy of the order.
commission_reply: The paper said it emailed the Commission and the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on 1 October and received no response.

what_happened: Hindustan Times reported that a security researcher emailed CERT-In on 8 July 2026, copied to the Commission's complaints address, about flaws in the voter-services website and the ECINET app. The worst, in the researcher's account, let anyone obtain election officials' names and mobile numbers without logging in.
commission_reply: HT said neither CERT-In nor the Commission answered its questions of 5 October. On 6 October CERT-In told the researcher that one flaw, the hardcoded encryption key he rated least serious, had been fixed and that work on the rest was under progress. HT said none of the flaws related directly to registration officers' access to the roll, and that the email alleged no theft or misuse of data.

what_happened: Congress alleged after the Hindustan Times report that ECINET was designed to centralise deletions and additions from the BJP's headquarters. This is a party's allegation. Hindustan Times had said none of the flaws it reported related directly to registration officers' access to the roll.
commission_reply: Scroll did not report a response from the Commission to this allegation.

what_happened: The security researcher who reported the ECINET flaws told The Wire that CERT-In and the Commission did not reply to him until a Hindustan Times reporter contacted them. CERT-In then said one issue had been resolved, which he said was the most minor. He said the flaws affected at least eight parts of the Commission's systems, including the Suvidha portal and ECORE.
commission_reply: No statement from the Commission was reported.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Form 7; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported, from more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 disclosures on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's website, that 87,127 deletion requests were filed by registration officers between 15 March and 2 April 2026 and that 85,854 of them gave no reason. Registration officers it spoke to said ERONET generated a Form 7 carrying their digital signature whenever they did not approve a voter at a hearing. It also reported that 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals were accepted after the deadline.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission had not replied by publication. On 13 October 2026 IANS reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office calling the claims misleading and saying "Notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders preceded action. Pending cases were decided after 6 March as per procedure."

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Electoral Registration Officer
issues: Software (ECINET/ERONET); Form 7; Names left off or deleted
what_happened: The Wire reported that 5,38,320 names were deleted from West Bengal's roll between the draft of December 2025 and the final roll of 28 February 2026 through Form 7s that the Commission's software generated in the officer's name when an officer did not approve an elector at a hearing, and that 7,733 more were deleted on Form 7s that people had filed. In the Form 10 registers it read for 284 of the 294 constituencies, 5,23,998 of 5,24,420 Form 7 deletions give the Electoral Registration Officer as the objector and leave the reason blank, and 422 give an individual objector. The Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 6 March 2026 said the state's Form 7 figure included these auto-generated forms, and that the Commission had sent the figure of 5,38,320 by email on 28 February.
commission_reply: The Wire reported that the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal told it Form 10 gives no option to record details, and that those deleted can apply again through Form 6.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer; Charchagram
what_happened: The Hindustan Times reported a review of ECINET's publicly served code by Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, which found an exception written into the code that can bar Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers in West Bengal from the View Enumeration Form Details tile on the SIR Phase II landing page and from the notice-and-hearing dashboard. The review found no such exclusion for these officers in any other state. The enumeration form page lists each form with its documents and the booth level officer's recommendation, and holds documents labelled as hearing orders. The review read only the code a browser receives before login, on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October and in code fetched on 19 October, so it cannot say whether the rule was ever used, whether the server enforces it, or when it was added. The paper could not verify the review independently.
commission_reply: The Hindustan Times reported that the Election Commission did not answer a questionnaire it sent.

what_happened: The Hindu reported another finding from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram. Behind the official login the portal has an area for managing State Nodal Officers, and each officer's row has a disable button whose confirmation says the user will no longer be able to access the application. Separately, the code carries the message that viewing enumeration form details is not enabled for the selected State, which the review reads as a feature switched on or off State by State. The review read only code the site serves before login. The paper says it was not clear since when the feature has been on the portal, which was launched in January 2026, and the reviewer said he had seen it since 28 September.
commission_reply: The Hindu carried a statement by the Congress general secretary (communications), Jairam Ramesh, that the ECINET system and the Commission's IT division had overruled the statutory authority of Electoral Registration Officers. It reported no response from the Commission.

what_happened: Millennium Post reported that the Trinamool Congress, reacting to the Hindustan Times report of the same day on the West Bengal rule in ECINET's code, asked the Election Commission who had authorised the Bengal-specific changes, why West Bengal was treated differently from other states, who is accountable and what safeguards protect every eligible voter's rights. The party also asked when the Chief Election Commissioner would take responsibility and resign.
commission_reply: The report carries no response from the Commission.

what_happened: The Wire reported three findings from Saurav Rajput's review of ECINET's code for the civic-tech initiative Charchagram, made on 2, 6, 7 and 9 October from code the site serves publicly, with no passwords and no use of ECINET's programming interfaces. Besides the State Nodal Officer controls and the West Bengal rule in the two reports before it, the review found code showing that the officials' portal marks some voters with a gold VIP symbol on the screen that shows the documents in an enumeration form, and a button that downloads a list of these VIP electors by Assembly constituency, which can be narrowed by state, district, constituency and polling part. The criteria for marking a voter are not known. The review cannot say whether any of these features were used, by whom or how often. The Reporters' Collective earlier reported a Mark VIP module in the booth level officers' app, and Charchagram says its review examined the other end of that chain.
commission_reply: The report carries no response from the Commission.

what_happened: In a reply dated 16 October to an RTI application from a social activist in Karimnagar, the Commission declined to give the name and version of the software it used to find errors and anomalies in the rolls during the revision, citing commercial confidence, trade secrets and intellectual property under Section 8(1)(d), the Hindustan Times reported. It called the questions on automatic flagging, artificial intelligence and safeguards against wrongful flagging a clarification outside the definition of information, and cited Section 8(1)(g) on who reviews flagged records.
commission_reply: The Commission said Electoral Registration Officers decide on including or excluding an elector on the basis of facts and records, and that under Sections 13B(1) and 13B(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 the officer of each constituency prepares and revises its roll.

what_happened: Lists of electors whose notices were still pending had been published for 39 of Maharashtra's 288 Assembly constituencies, in 14 districts, on the election authorities' websites by Saturday 24 October, The Times of India reported. Officials said the lists hold only unresolved cases and do not cover all 1.22 crore notices generated in the revision. In Pune district only the Shivajinagar list was up, with one elector on it, and in Mumbai the lists for Malabar Hill, Byculla, Dharavi, Dahisar and Vandre West. A circular of 23 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office told electoral registration officers to download the data from the Commission's ECINET platform, compile one PDF for each constituency, publish it on the district election officer's website by 26 October and share part-wise lists with parties' booth level agents. Officials said documents some electors had given booth level officers during enumeration were not uploaded because the system did not support it then. Notices are to be disposed of by 10 November and the final roll is due on 16 November.
commission_reply: An electoral official said a name on the list does not mean the elector has been finally deleted from the roll, and the report says the Chief Electoral Officer's office will review whether district election authorities have complied with the circular.

what_happened: Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission asking it to change Form 6 so that electors left off the draft in the revision can register again without declaring themselves first-time voters, Deccan Chronicle reported. The letter says officers find it hard to persuade such electors to sign a form that carries a penalty for a false declaration. It asks for the words "new voters" to be taken out of the form's title, for a separate declaration for people who were enrolled before and are no longer on any roll, and for a place to give the earlier EPIC number.
commission_reply: Officials said that any change to the statutory Form 6 would need the Central government to amend the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. No decision by the Commission was reported.

what_happened: The BBC reported that voters in villages near Patna told it the Bihar draft roll carried wrong photographs, duplicate entries and the name of a person who died more than five years earlier. commission_reply: In response to the BBC's questions, the Election Commission shared its 24 June order on conducting the SIR and a 27 July press note outlining efforts to ensure no eligible voter was "left behind". The BBC also noted the commission has said BLOs worked "very responsibly".

Booth officers told the paper the instruction reached them orally or on WhatsApp and that they had seen no formal order. One registration officer's message asked them to visit every elector marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate within seven days and take Form 6 from any found living at the address. what_happened: The Uttar Pradesh Congress alleged at a press conference in Lucknow that in Pilibhit Sadar the names of 13,150 voters were changed between July and September, after the final roll of 10 April 2026, while their EPIC and serial numbers stayed the same, PTI reported. The party said 884 names of people still living there were deleted and 2,600 names of people who did not live there were added, and that the changes appeared to have been made in batches. It asked for an inquiry and said it would go to court. These are the Congress's allegations.
commission_reply: The report carries no response. The next day The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, after an inquiry found that searching some EPIC numbers online showed other voters' details, had ordered the constituency's Electoral Registration Officer and Voter Registration Centre operator off roll duties and legal action against them.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh; BJP; AAP
what_happened: Voter slips for the Legislative Council election in the Allahabad-Jhansi graduates' constituency, where polling was set for 23 October, carried Hindi phrases in place of electors' and fathers' names, and pictures of them spread on social media before the polling parties left, Dainik Jagran reported. On the instructions of the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, the Returning Officer, Bimal Kumar Dubey, who is Divisional Commissioner of Jhansi, had the roll checked and reported clerical errors and more than 100 duplicate names. The Bharatiya Janata Party separately complained to the Chief Electoral Officer that the roll held 4,397 duplicate electors, and that electors born between 2001 and 2005 were on it whom the party called too young to qualify. The party's Prayagraj city president put 3,163 of the duplicates in Prayagraj.
commission_reply: The Returning Officer said in a press note of 17 October that no elector would be denied the vote because of a clerical error, and that an elector whose identity satisfied the presiding officer or polling officer would be allowed to vote. The report says the clerical errors found in the check were marked and corrected, and that a separate list of the duplicate names was being given to the presiding officers of the polling stations concerned, with instructions to keep a special watch on those names during the poll. The Indian Express reported on 26 October that the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, replied on X to the Aam Aadmi Party's Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, who had asked the Chief Election Commissioner why a voter slip read “Ram ne Yadav ko Maara” and whether the Commission's computer was casteist. The reply said the roll of the recent Legislative Council election also carried the entry “Ram ne Sharma ko Maara”, and the office shared a slip from the graduates' constituency election with that phrase in place of an elector's father's name. The paper quotes Rinwa as saying “Computers/software are not casteist” and “We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism.”

what_happened: An FIR was lodged on 22 October against the two Sub-Divisional Magistrates who had served as Pilibhit's Electoral Registration Officers and a computer operator at the constituency's Voter Registration Centre, under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, The Wire reported. The Chief Electoral Officer's inquiry found that the operator had entered 13,779 Form 8 applications to change voters' details between 31 May and 29 August 2026, of which 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected, and that the office held no forms or records for any of them. The two officers were moved to district headquarters and the operator's services were ended. The District Election Officer was told to examine every Form 6 and Form 7 entry made by the same operator from 10 April to 21 October.
commission_reply: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. Officials said the entries found irregular were being corrected, and the District Magistrate said the rolls of every constituency in the district would be cleaned up in a day or two.

what_happened: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, took five booth level officers and a computer assistant off all roll work on 24 October and began ending their services, after an inquiry into the roll of the Azamgarh Assembly constituency (347), The Hindu reported. The Samajwadi Party had said at a press conference that one elector's name appeared ten times on that roll. The District Election Officer's report found the name 13 times in Hindi. Two of the entries had been taken up for deletion, and the other 11 belonged to 11 different people living in Azamgarh, ten of whose names and details were being corrected through Form 8. The Chief Electoral Officer ordered charge sheets and departmental proceedings against the Electoral Registration Officer of the time and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers, with action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and asked for a report on the rolls of every constituency in the district within a week.
commission_reply: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. His office said a further entry with the same name, in the Chauri Chaura constituency of Gorakhpur district, belonged to a different elector. The Indian Express quoted him saying the three officers would face action for negligence and laxity in supervision while the roll was prepared.

issues: Duplicates and errors; Form 6; Form 7; Form 8; Software (ECINET/ERONET)
what_happened: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, ordered on 25 October that every Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 entered by computer assistants between the final roll of 10 April and 24 October be checked again, after the errors found in the rolls of Pilibhit and Azamgarh, The Indian Express reported. Computer assistants may no longer enter forms received on paper, which booth level officers are to digitise through the BLO App. Electoral Registration Officers are to review pending forms every day, and officials were told not to share their ERONET login IDs and passwords, were directed to study Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which deals with breaches of official duty in preparing the roll, and were warned of strict action. The office pulled up the District Election Officers of Bulandshahr, Sitapur, Ghaziabad and Aligarh for late reports on complaints of duplicate voters circulated on social media, and directed that the draft rolls of the coming Special Summary Revision carry no duplicate entries.
commission_reply: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. They followed a virtual meeting with Divisional Commissioners, District Election Officers, registration officers and computer assistants, held to prepare for the Special Summary Revision, which The Hindu dates 24 October. The Hindu reports the same directions from an official statement, says officials were warned of action under Section 32, and adds that the section provides for imprisonment of at least three months and up to two years, with a fine.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; Police; Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu
what_happened: The Indian Express reported the deaths of two BLOs. The family of a BLO in Kannur, Kerala, alleged he was under pressure to finish by December 4, and police said a note found on a BLO in Jaipur said he faced extreme pressure from his supervisor and was told he would be suspended if he did not meet his SIR target. It also reported that revenue employees in Tamil Nadu announced a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload.
commission_reply: Kannur District Collector Arun K Vijayan's report indicated that the BLO was not under any work pressure. The Indian Express said its multiple calls and messages to Rajasthan CEO Naveen got no response.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; District Election Officer
what_happened: The Indian Express reported that two women assistant BLOs died of heart attacks in Tapi and Vadodara districts, bringing BLO deaths in Gujarat that week to four. The husband of one said she was a heart patient who had asked to be excused from BLO duty, which the Vadodara Collector disputed.
commission_reply: Vadodara District Collector Anil Dhameliya said, “We checked with the institute as well as with the local officials. She had not made any official request to be excused (from BLO duty)… We have learnt now that she was suffering from a heart ailment and had episodes of fainting in her institute as well.” He also said, “We have been cautious about ensuring that there is no excessive workload on the BLOs and therefore, we have appointed additional staff to assist in the process.” An unnamed government official said, “With a large workforce of over two lakh involved in the SIR work, these deaths can be termed as natural. Linking these to SIR is not justified and logical.”

parties_and_bodies: Police; Electoral Registration Officer; Booth level officers
issues: Deaths; BLO workload; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The New Indian Express reported four deaths of officers on revision duty in Uttar Pradesh that families tied to workload. They were a lekhpal supervisor in Fatehpur who died by suicide a day before his wedding, after what his family said were threats of dismissal, a teacher who collapsed on duty in Bareilly, a teacher in Gonda who died by suicide and an officer in Lucknow who had a brain haemorrhage. In Fatehpur police registered an FIR for abetment against a revenue officer and unnamed officials.
commission_reply: The paper reported, citing unnamed sources, that the family had first named the electoral registration officer and was made to change the complaint, which the Additional Superintendent of Police, Fatehpur, denied.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Booth level officers; Election Commission

what_happened: A 46-year-old assistant teacher on booth officer duty since 7 October died by suicide at home in Moradabad, police said, leaving a note to the district Basic Education Officer saying he could not meet the SIR targets, India Today reported.
commission_reply: The District Magistrate said "Preliminary information suggests he died by suicide. His quality of work was excellent. Anganwadi employees were deployed to assist him. Both administrative and police probes are underway." The Commission extended the SIR schedule by a week the same day.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Booth level officers
what_happened: A 40-year-old assistant teacher working as a booth officer in Hathras collapsed at home and died on the way to hospital, The Telegraph reported. His family said he had been under stress since starting the work. The paper counted three booth officer deaths in Uttar Pradesh since the previous Sunday.
commission_reply: The District Magistrate called the death unfortunate, said the cause would be clear after the post-mortem, and said the administration would explore a job for the officer's wife.

what_happened: The BBC reported that 10 BLOs it spoke to in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal said they worked 14 to 15 hours a day with little rest, and that families linked the deaths of more than a dozen poll workers, by alleged suicide or heart attack, to election work stress. The BBC said it had not independently verified the causes of death. It reported BLOs saying the SIR app crashed often and that many had not been paid.
commission_reply: The BBC said the Commission did not answer its questions. It cited media reports of a court affidavit in which the Commission called claims linking booth officers' deaths to the revision "false, exaggerated and politically motivated".

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that a 75-year-old man died of cardiac arrest, according to hospital sources, after falling ill in a queue for an SIR hearing at the Rampurhat-1 block office in Birbhum. His wife and family alleged the SIR process had caused him excessive stress and held the Election Commission responsible. It also reported that an elderly man died of cardiac arrest at an SIR hearing in Howrah the previous day.

what_happened: The New Indian Express, citing PTI, reported that police in Purulia registered an FIR on a complaint by the son of an 82-year-old man who died allegedly by suicide on 29 December hours before he was due at an SIR hearing. An officer was quoted as saying the case included charges of abetment of suicide and criminal conspiracy against Election Commission officials, with no official named. The family alleged he acted out of anxiety over the SIR.
